title: No in-game logic editor: processor code cannot be viewed or edited; tapping a processor opens a dead one-line field

java: Open Mindustry, enter a custom game, place a micro-processor, tap it -> the full-screen LogicDialog/LCanvas opens with the code editor and Add-statement UI (LogicBlock.java:737-760).
Type a program and press OK -> the processor stores and runs it (compressed byte[] config).
Editor: open the map's World Processors dialog -> each row has edit/name/icon/delete actions plus Add (MapProcessorsDialog.java:47-120).
godot: Launch the Godot client, custom game, place a micro-processor, tap it -> a block config panel with a single-line `LineEdit` (block_config_fragment.gd:64).

Type `set x 1` and press OK -> nothing is stored: configure_building maps the kind to ConfigValue::String (input/mod.rs:877-885) and LogicBlockBehavior ignores String for non-privileged processors (logic_block.rs:539-548).
grep client/ui + client/scenes for MindLogic consumers -> none; dialogs_manifest.json has no `logic` entry and client/ui/dialogs/ has no logic dialog.
compare: Java opens the full-screen LogicDialog with the LCanvas editor; Godot opens a one-line LineEdit that cannot set code.
Java submits compressed code bytes; the Godot UI has no bytes-capable config kind (only none/string/content/number/bool) and the only caller sends string/content/none.

Java's editor World Processors dialog can add/rename/icon/delete/edit processors; the Godot dialog only lists tag rows (map_processors_dialog.gd:47-64) and MindEditor.processors() (editor/mod.rs:900) is read-only.
MindLogic already exposes statement metadata/counts 'for the plan-14 logic editor' (logic.rs:7) but no shim consumes it.

2. Stop routing LogicBlock taps to the one-line field: in DesktopBridge::config_spec (desktop.rs:1400) emit an open-logic effect for BlockKind::LogicBlock instead of `text:true`; have MindInput open the new dialog seeded with the tile and current code (read through a real logic_get_state).
3. Add a bytes/logic kind to configure_building (input/mod.rs:874-896) that encodes via logic_block::compress + relative_connections (logic_block.rs:485, 419) and sends ConfigValue::Bytes; LogicBlockBehavior::configured already applies Bytes (logic_block.rs:530-538).
4. Keep String config as the world-processor name action only (logic_block.rs:539), and port CanvasEditDialog (CanvasBlock.java:311) plus the MapProcessorsDialog add/edit/delete rows (map_processors_dialog.gd:47, editor/mod.rs:900) onto the same dialog with forceEditor.
5. Replace the sim_host.rs:718-740 probe stubs (logic_place/logic_set_code/logic_get_state/logic_display_commands) with real place/configure/read so the editor, the MCP oracle and the evaluator share one seam.

In-engine: place a processor, open the new editor, type a program, OK, then `SimHost.logic_get_state(x,y)` returns the code and vars (today `{}`).

title: World-processor side effects never happen: messages, effects, setrule, flags and sounds stay inert in the live client

java: World processor program `message notify "hi"` -> the toast appears immediately (LExecutor.java:1917).
`setrule waves false` disables waves, `effect ...` spawns FX, `explosion ...` damages, `playsound ...` plays (LExecutor.java:1779, 1975).
godot: Load/place a world processor with a program ending in `message notify "hi"` (via an imported map/save or the harness) and run it -> no toast appears.
SimHost.logic_set_rule returns false (sim_host.rs:751) and no LogicWorldState resource exists on the live Sim: install_sim_seams (sim_host.rs:289-306) installs GlobalVars and AudioSinkRes only.

With the resource absent every privileged run_* early-returns (world.rs:1101 setrule, 1208 effect, 1285 setflag, 1400 playsound); even with it installed, LogicWorldState.events is only read by the headless scenario reporter (logic_scenarios.rs:1344) and headless defaults true (world.rs:396), so run_flush_message swallows messages (world.rs:1116-1122).
compare: Java world instructions mutate state/ui/audio directly each tick; the port records LogicWorldEvent on LogicWorldState (or silently drops the instruction when the resource is missing) and no client-side consumer drains them.
Java's message blocking uses ui.hasAnnouncement/hasToast; the port has MessageState but nothing installs or updates it.

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
plan.seam: MindSimHost::install_sim_seams (sim_host.rs:289) does not install LogicWorldState and no host drains LogicWorldState.events into the view/audio/FX/sim sinks.
plan.approach:
1. Install `LogicWorldState { is_host: true, headless: false, .. }` on the live Sim in MindSimHost::install_sim_seams (sim_host.rs:289-306; also after load_sector at :1004), refreshed per tick with state.tick/wave/wavetime and grid dims.
2. Add a once-per-tick drain of LogicWorldState.events (world.rs:405) in the host: Message -> MindUi announce/toast with duration (FlushMessageI semantics, LExecutor.java:1917); Effect -> MindFx FxBus; PlaySound/PlayMusic -> the AudioSinkRes/AudioEvent path; SetBlock -> SimRuntime::place/break; SpawnUnit/SpawnBullet/ApplyStatus/Explosion -> the unit/combat runtime; Cutscene -> MindCamera2D; Flag/Mission -> CampaignRuntime; Sync/ClientData -> the MindNet relay.
3. Reconcile setrule: run_set_rule only mutates the scratch LogicWorldState.rules (world.rs:1084-1103), so the drain must map the changed rules onto the live Rules/session (and emit a matching event).
4. Wire MessageState.has_announcement/has_toast so the `@wait` blocking branch in run_flush_message can proceed (world.rs:1124-1142).
plan.narrow_check: mind-core test: install the block runtime + a host-installed LogicWorldState(headless=false), assemble a privileged program `message notify "hi"`, tick, assert exactly one LogicWorldEvent::Message is emitted and consumed by a test sink. In-engine: run the same processor and assert MindUi's toast/announce signal fires (today nothing happens and SimHost.logic_set_rule is a false stub).

note: Code-scan 2026-10-10 (logic): S2/high - the whole privileged instruction surface is dead in the live client for two reasons (missing LogicWorldState resource; no event drain), so logic-driven messages/effects/rules/audio never reach the player. Authored code must currently arrive via an imported map/save until the logic editor lands (see logic-editor item). In-engine verification pending.

title: Logic displays stay blank: drawflush output is never rendered and tileable displays never link into one canvas

java: Place a logic-display plus a processor running `draw clear 255 0 0 0` and `drawflush display1` -> the display turns red (LogicDisplay.java:98 draw -> :158 processCommands).
Place a 2x2 tile-logic-display -> the BFS links it into one framebuffer with a bottom-left root (TileableLogicDisplay.java:39).
`draw image x y display1 ...` packs the source display's root index (LExecutor.java:1009).
godot: Same rig -> the display stays visually blank: no render pass or host code reads LogicDisplayState.commands (grep found no consumer in mind-gdext) and MindSimHost.logic_display_commands returns an empty array (sim_host.rs:738).
Sim side still appends packed commands per flush_draw (io.rs:305-328) and increments operations, so the data exists but is never drawn.

Tileable: DisplayBehavior::create_state only sets root_display=Some(self) (display.rs:73-89) and `root_display` is never reassigned anywhere; the BFS/needsUpdate/origin fields are absent. `draw image` from a display packs only the sentinel 30 and drops the root index (draw.rs:251-256).
compare: Java renders the packed DisplayCmd queue through a FrameBuffer and links tileable displays; the port records the queue but has no consumer, no framebuffer and no tileable link.
Java message blocks draw their stored text (MessageBlock.java:77 drawSelect); MessageBlockState has no consumer either (same missing host-consume family).

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
plan.seam: Missing host display-command consumer/render pass (plan-16 `render`) plus the TileableLogicDisplay BFS link and root-index resolution in the sim.
plan.approach:
1. Implement the host half of LogicDisplay: a render pass that reads LogicDisplayState.commands and replays the DisplayCmd stream with the draw.rs decoders (COMMAND_* / unpack_sign) into a per-display texture (SubViewport or ImageTexture) mounted at the block center, i.e. the upstream processCommands/draw pair (LogicDisplay.java:98,158); add it to the plan-16 BandPlan in client/rust/mind-gdext/src/render.rs and make MindSimHost.logic_display_commands (:738) return the real queue.
2. Port TileableLogicDisplay.linkDisplays (Java :39-110): on place/break of a tileable display, BFS the proximity graph to the bottom-left root, store root_display/tiles_width/tiles_height/origin/rectangular/needs_update on LogicDisplayState, and route flushes to the root.
3. Fix `draw image` from a display source: pack `(root.index << 5) | 30` in pack_draw's Building branch (draw.rs:251-256) like LExecutor.java:1009, and have flush_draw target the root display (io.rs:305).
4. Consume MessageBlockState in the same host pass (draw the stored text over the block; MessageBlock.java:77).
plan.narrow_check: mind-core test: place a 2x2 tile-logic-display and assert all four entities share one root and `draw image ... display1` packs (root.index<<5)|30. In-engine: processor `draw clear 255 0 0 0` + `drawflush display1` next to a logic-display -> capture the viewport and assert red pixels on the display tile (today blank); repeat with the tileable display.

note: Code-scan 2026-10-10 (logic): S2/high - displays are dead output: the sim records commands but nothing consumes them, tileable displays never link (root_display fixed to self) and commandImage resolution drops the root index, so even a future renderer would misaddress multi-display sources. In-engine verification pending.

title: Processors read frozen globals: @tick/@time/@wave never advance in the live client

java: Processor `set t @tick` then print/sense t -> t increases every tick; @time/@second/@wave/@waveNumber/@mapw/@maph/@server/@client all track live state (GlobalVars.java:192-230).
godot: Same program in the live client -> t stays 0 forever: @tick is initialized to 0 (globals.rs:192) and GlobalVars::update/update_world has no caller outside mind-headless (only logic_scenarios.rs:145); Sim::tick (sim/mod.rs:383-398) never touches globals.
Executor::refresh_globals (executor/mod.rs:1813-1834) reads the ECS GlobalVars resource every run, so the stale values are exactly what a running processor observes.
compare: Java Logic.update() calls logicVars.update() every frame/tick (Logic.java:546) and the values feed LVar.numval directly; the port's live tick path has no GlobalUpdate at all.

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
plan.seam: Sim tick / GlobalVars: no per-tick GlobalUpdate in the live path (host wiring), executor read side is ready.
plan.approach:
1. Build a GlobalUpdate from live sim state each tick (in Sim::tick around sim/mod.rs:383-398, or a dedicated scheduled system in sim/schedule.rs): tick from state.tick, wave/wavetime from the campaign session (CampaignRuntime/session), mapw/maph from the grid, server/client from host role, plus client locale/mobile/music from settings/audio where available.
2. Call GlobalVars::update_world (globals.rs:343-348) with it; the existing refresh_globals mirror path (executor/mod.rs:1813) then feeds every running processor with no executor change.
3. Re-run the wiring after Sim replacement in install_sim_seams (sim_host.rs:289) / load_sector (:1004) so loaded sectors get it too.
plan.narrow_check: New mind-core sim test: install the block runtime + GlobalVars, place a processor running `set t @tick`, tick 120, assert t==120 (currently 0). The headless `logic_globals_live` scenario (logic_scenarios.rs:103) already asserts the same contract for the harness path.

note: Code-scan 2026-10-10 (logic): S3/high - every processor reading time/wave/map globals gets install-time constants (all 0) instead of live values; logic programs using @tick/@time for delays or @server/@client for host detection are wrong. In-engine verification pending.

title: `lookup` returns null for every id (mlog content-by-id lookups always fail)

java: Processor `lookup block 1 r` then `print r` -> prints the resolved block name; unit/item/liquid/team lookups resolve through GlobalVars.lookupContent (GlobalVars.java:237-245).
godot: Same program -> r is null: the run branch always writes a null object (executor/mod.rs:1066-1071).
The lowering already drops the content type (`Statement::Lookup { result, id, .. }`, executor/mod.rs:2055-2059) even though Statement::Lookup carries type/from fields (statement.rs:274).
compare: Java resolves (type,id) through logicIdToContent; the port stores nothing and returns null for every id.

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
plan.seam: Executor Lookup branch + lowering; needs an id->content table resource (dense content ids or logicids ordering).
plan.approach:
1. Preserve the content type through lowering: add `type_: ContentType` to Instruction::Lookup (executor/mod.rs:2055) from Statement::Lookup's type field (statement.rs:274).
2. Add an id->ContentRef table per lookable type (the dense per-type ids the ContentRegistry already assigns, extended from ContentIndex in sim/runtime.rs:91 or installed like LogicContentIndex in world/generation.rs) and resolve in the Lookup run branch (executor/mod.rs:1066) as `lookupContent(type, id)`; keep the team special case (GlobalVars.java:237-241) via the team registry.
3. Return null only for unknown/out-of-range ids; leave all other statements untouched.
plan.narrow_check: mind-core test: assemble `lookup block 1 r` + `sensor r @id s` (or compare the LogicObject::Content) and assert the resolved ContentRef matches the registry's id 1 for that type (today null).

title: Tapping a switch opens an empty config panel and never toggles it (no Boolean config path)

java: Place a switch and tap it -> configure(!enabled) toggles it immediately (SwitchBlock.java:58-61) and the enabled sprite/sense changes.
godot: Place a switch and tap it -> a config panel with only Clear and X (config_spec returns options=[] and text=false because SwitchBehavior declares no Bool config kind), and the switch's enabled state never changes.
configure_building (input/mod.rs:874-896) can map kind=bool, but no GDScript path sends it: block_config_fragment.gd only submits string (line 72), content (99) and none (88).
compare: Java declares config(Boolean.class) on SwitchBlock (SwitchBlock.java:28) and toggles on tap; the port has the sim-side Bool handler (switch.rs:31-36) but no declared kind, no tap toggle and no UI submit path.
Linked processors therefore always read `switch1` as disabled.
